name: NJ-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's +27 Democratic partisan lean makes a Republican win extremely unlikely
McIver holds a massive fundraising edge ($2.1M raised vs. $2.3K for Bucco) with no outside opposition spending
Prediction markets price McIver at 99% to win
Incumbent running for re-election adds a small further advantage
model.rationale: This Newark-area seat leans Democratic by 27 points, incumbent LaMonica McIver has out-raised Carmen Bucco by roughly a thousand to one, and markets give her a 99% chance of winning. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting any competition, the fundamentals alone point to an easy Democratic hold.
model.watch: Any late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending could narrow the margin, though it would take an extraordinary shift to put the seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
LaMonica McIver, the Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored to win re-election in New Jersey's 10th District. The district leans Democratic by 27 points, and no independent ratings or public polls treat the race as competitive. Prediction markets price McIver's chances at 99 percent.

The financial picture is lopsided: McIver has raised about $2.1 million and holds over $800,000 on hand, while Republican Carmen Bucco has raised roughly $2,300 with about $1,000 available. There is no outside spending against the incumbent. Barring an unforeseen development, this seat is expected to remain safely in Democratic hands.
